newsitem.title: USA: Arrow Air to begin scheduled Peru service.
newsitem.headline: Arrow Air to begin scheduled Peru service.

text.p: Arrow Air Inc, the Miami all-cargo airline, will initiate scheduled service to Peru within the next couple of weeks, a senior executive told Reuters Monday.
"We are very interested in Peru," Jon Batchelor, senior vice president, said in an interview.
"We do not see any problem" with meeting the December 2 deadline set by The Department of Transportation when it granted Arrow authority to fly to Peru in September, he said.

The department also granted twice weekly all-cargo flights to Florida West International, which had not yet been certified to fly by the Federal Aviation Administration. Millon Air, which has been grounded since its October 22 crash in Ecuador, was awarded authority to fly twice weekly.
Arrow has been flying charter service to Peru. But Batchelor said its twice weekly scheduled service would be new.
Arrow opened a Houston sales office and expects cargo to be trucked from there to Miami for flights to Peru, he said.
"Southbound (to Peru) it is general hard freight and northbound we get a lot of asparagus," he said.

Arrow flew the sixth most international cargo through Miami International Airport and Millon the ninth most in the first nine months of 1996, according to statistics compiled by Dade County Aviation Department.

DOT was to have awarded additional thrice weekly frequencies that became available November 1, but is holding off until it sees how the market responds to the twice weekly service, according to DOT spokesman Bill Mosley.

Florida West will be allowed to miss the December 2 deadline pending its FAA certification, Mosley said. Million will likely also be given this consideration if they are not in the air by December 2, he said.
